scenarios.title: Training: navigation, picking and comparing
scenarios.question: Training (about 3 min). Pan, orbit and zoom; hover a cell to see its values; click to select it; select a cell and press C, then another cell and press C, to compare them as A and B. Say aloud what you see. No answer needed.

scenarios.title: Population density and income
scenarios.question: A municipality is conducting an initial assessment of population concentration and socioeconomic differences across the city. Compare two selected grid cells. Which area has the higher population density? How do their income levels differ? Based on these two indicators, what differences between the areas appear relevant for further investigation?
scenarios.instruction: The two cells are marked A and B and shown side by side in the comparison panel. Use it and the info panel for exact values and ranks.

scenarios.title: Income and foreign-born population
scenarios.question: A municipality wants to better understand the socioeconomic and demographic characteristics of different neighbourhoods. Compare two selected DeSO areas. How do their income levels and shares of residents born abroad differ? What might these differences suggest for further municipal analysis, and what cannot be concluded from these area-level statistics alone?

scenarios.question: A municipality is conducting an initial assessment of neighbourhood characteristics. Compare two selected grid cells. scenarios.title: Sweden Democrats and foreign-born population
scenarios.question: A municipality is examining how electoral patterns vary across neighbourhoods with different demographic characteristics. Identify an area where the Sweden Democrats have relatively high electoral support and compare it with another selected area. How does SD vote share differ between the areas? How does the share of residents born abroad differ? Looking at the wider spatial pattern, does the relationship appear consistent or mixed? What conclusions cannot be made about individual voters from these data?
scenarios.instruction: Area B is already selected. Put your own area into A: select a district and press C.
scenarios.instructionVr: Area B is already selected. Put your own area into A: choose Compare on the table toolbar and click a district.

scenarios.title: Vänsterpartiet vs Socialdemokraterna and foreign-born population
scenarios.question: A municipality wants to explore how support for Vänsterpartiet and Socialdemokraterna varies across neighbourhoods with different demographic profiles. Find an area where Vänsterpartiet is relatively strong and inspect its foreign-born population share. Switch to the Socialdemokraterna layer while keeping the same location and compare the parties. Repeat the comparison for a second area. Where is V relatively stronger and where is S relatively stronger? How does this relate spatially to foreign-born population share, and what cannot be concluded about how individual residents voted?
scenarios.instruction: Put your V area into A (select a district and press C); the second area, B, is already selected. "Switch view" changes the colour between V and S; geometry, heights and the 0–50 % colour scale stay the same. "Relatively stronger" = higher compared with the party's result in the whole municipality.
scenarios.instructionVr: Put your V area into A (Compare on the toolbar, then click a district); the second area, B, is already selected. The switch button changes the colour between V and S; geometry, heights and the 0–50 % colour scale stay the same. "Relatively stronger" = higher compared with the party's result in the whole municipality.
